title: ～たばかり — “just ～ed”
summary: Attached to the ta-form of a verb, it shows that not much time has passed since the action. If the speaker feels it was “just now”, it may actually be days or months ago.

patterns.gloss: Verb ta-form + ばかり (着いたばかり)

body.p: Use it when, in the speaker’s feeling, the action is still fresh. A result or state often follows: 入社したばかりで慣れていない.
たばかり depends on the speaker’s sense and can cover days or months. たところ is limited to the moments right after the action ends.

examples.ja: 今（いま）、駅（えき）に着（つ）いたばかりです。
examples.romaji: Ima, eki ni tsuita bakari desu.
examples.tr: I just arrived at the station now.

examples.ja: この会社（かいしゃ）に入（はい）ったばかりで、まだ慣（な）れていない。
examples.romaji: Kono kaisha ni haitta bakari de, mada narete inai.
examples.tr: I just joined this company, so I'm not used to it yet.

examples.ja: 買（か）ったばかりの傘（かさ）をなくしてしまった。
examples.romaji: Katta bakari no kasa o nakushite shimatta.
examples.tr: I lost the umbrella I had just bought.

pitfalls: Attach it to the ta-form (着いたばかり).
It is not for an action in progress; it describes the time after it finished.
